```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(PGViS)
```

This is the first of a series that walks the whole pipeline one step at a
time. Here we do the unglamorous but load-bearing part: telling PGViS where
everything lives, and making sure the three external reference resources are
actually present before you commit a cluster to a multi-day run.

## Everything hangs off one config object

A pipeline like this touches a lot of paths, and it's easy for them to end up
sprinkled through the code where changing machines means hunting them all
down. PGViS keeps every path, threshold and tool location in one object, and
nothing else is allowed to hard-code them.

```{r config}
cfg <- pgvis_config(
  root      = file.path(tempdir(), "demo_project"),
  cohorts   = c("luad", "lusc")
)
cfg
```

`root` is the only thing you must supply. Under it, PGViS lays out a fixed,
numbered directory tree — stage 1 writes to `01_bam`, stage 2 to `02_gvcf`,
and so on down to `10_score` — so you always know where a given stage's output
lives.

```{r dirs}
cfg$dirs$gvcf
cfg$dirs$score
```

Create the tree on disk with `pgvis_init()`:

```{r init}
pgvis_init(cfg)
dir.exists(cfg$dirs$score)
```

## Thresholds are configuration, not code edits

The disruption thresholds live in the config rather than being edited into the
code, so the settings that produced a given result travel with the project
instead of having to be remembered. They come with sensible defaults.

```{r thresholds}
strict <- pgvis_config(
  root = tempdir(),
  thresholds = list(ref_prob_min = 0.7, alt_prob_max = 0.3)
)
strict$thresholds
```

Note that the two values you didn't set kept their defaults rather than
vanishing — `thresholds` is merged with the defaults, not replaced by your
list. The full set:

- `ref_prob_min` / `alt_prob_max` — how confident the model must be that the
  reference sequence *is* a functional element and the mutated one is *not*
- `min_carrier_frac` — the "enriched in ≥ 5% of patients" floor
- `max_indel_len` — longest allele kept (10 bp)
- `pseudocount` — added to frequencies before ratios
- `drop_freq_sources` — population sources to exclude when scoring; defaults
  to `"1000G"` so a 1000 Genomes reference is never compared against
  1000G-derived frequencies

## The three reference resources

PGViS needs a genome FASTA (for variant calling and sequence extraction), the
dbSnp155 frequency track (for population allele frequencies), and one BED per
regulatory region you want to test. The canonical download locations are
built in:

```{r urls}
urls <- pgvis_reference_urls("hg38")
urls$dbsnp155_common
urls$genome_fasta
```

These point at the UCSC download server, which matters: the frequency parsing
in PGViS was built against the layout of UCSC's dbSnp155 track. A different
dbSNP build, or the raw NCBI VCF, packs the per-population frequencies
differently and will silently break the lookup.

### Preparing dbSNP

The track ships as one binary bigBed. PGViS splits it into the per-chromosome
BEDs the intersection stage reads. You can see exactly what it will run
before committing to the download:

```{r dbsnp-dry}
pgvis_prepare_dbsnp(
  dest        = file.path(cfg$root, "dbsnp"),
  subset      = "common",          # far smaller than "all"; enough for most work
  chromosomes = c("21", "22"),
  dry_run     = TRUE
)
```

Dropping `dry_run` runs it for real (it needs UCSC's `bigBedToBed` on your
`PATH`, or its path passed as `bigbedtobed`). Extraction is per-chromosome
straight from the bigBed, so you never materialise the whole multi-gigabyte
track. Like every long-running step in PGViS, it skips chromosomes that are
already done, so an interrupted download is just restarted.

## Check before you launch

The single most useful habit: verify the references resolve *before* queuing
the pipeline, not six hours in when a job dies looking for a missing `.fai`.

```{r check}
pgvis_check_references(cfg)
```

Everything is flagged here because this demo config points at nothing real.
On a configured project each line reads `[OK]`, and only then is it worth
submitting stage 1.

## What can go wrong

- **`cfg$reference_fasta` unset.** Variant calling and sequence extraction
  both need it; PGViS refuses to start those stages without it.
- **dbSNP build mismatch.** If most variants later come back with
  `freq_source == "none"`, the usual cause is a dbSNP track that isn't UCSC
  dbSnp155, so the frequency-column indices in `pgvis_freq_sources()` point at
  the wrong fields. `pgvis_qc()` (covered in vignette 5) flags this explicitly.
- **Region BEDs on the wrong genome.** A hg19 region BED against hg38 variants
  intersects to almost nothing. `pgvis_check_references()` confirms the files
  exist but cannot know their build — that one is on you.
